# Hardware

The laboratory combines centralized instructor-managed infrastructure with individual student equipment sets, using reusable and readily available networking and computing equipment.

## Central Server Cart

![VoIP Laboratory — Central Server Cart](voip-central-server-cart.png)

*Figure 1. Central mobile platform integrating the FreePBX/Asterisk server, Ethernet switching, routing, SIP endpoint, and local administration console.*

The central platform provides the shared provider/interconnection network. It includes a dedicated Linux/FreePBX/Asterisk server, a multiport Ethernet switch, a laboratory router separating the school network from `172.16.0.0/16`, and a physical SIP/IP phone for demonstrations and testing.

## Student Equipment Set

![VoIP Laboratory — Student Equipment Set](voip-student-equipment-set.png)

*Figure 2. Student equipment set with laptop, dedicated router, and physical SIP/IP telephone.*

Each student receives:

- a laptop used for configuration, VirtualBox, PBX administration, and a softphone;
- a dedicated router providing WAN/LAN separation, DHCP, NAT, routing, and port forwarding;
- a physical SIP/IP desk telephone;
- and a mobile device that can run an additional SIP softphone.

The student therefore operates a complete independent VoIP network rather than sharing a single classroom PBX.

## Equipment Reuse and Replication

The laboratory does not depend on a specialized commercial VoIP training platform. Standard computers, Ethernet switches, routers, IP phones, virtualization software, and open-source PBX software are combined to reproduce the technical functions required by the learning activities.

Equivalent equipment can be substituted when it preserves the same student workflow and functional relationships.
